content.thinking: Given notice served 10 October by email, the two-month period runs to 10 December 2026, which I'll treat as the safe end date unless the landlord agrees in writing to something earlier. I should draft messages to both tenant and landlord with follow-up reminders, and on the keys issue I shouldn't invent an address—I'll just note they'll be returned to the agency office at checkout and confirm later.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for your email of 10 October, we've logged your notice. Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. The earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due until then. You asked for 10 November, so we're asking your landlord whether he'll agree to that in writing. Until he does, please plan on 10 December. We'll tell you his answer once we have it, and we'll update you by Wednesday 14 October at the latest. We're starting your move-out now. We'll arrange a checkout inspection close to your end date, and we'll write with the date. You'll hand the keys back to us at checkout, and we'll confirm exactly where and how then. Please don't post them. Your deposit (£2,019) is protected with mydeposits. It is returned after checkout once any deductions are agreed, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. Any agreed amount is paid within 10 days. Good luck with the new job in Manchester! Please send us your forwarding address.

Hi Ben, Tom Achterberg at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road gave notice by email on 10 October, asking to leave on 10 November (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act he needs to give two months' notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026. Please tell us whether you'll accept 10 November, or another earlier date, in writing. If you don't, the tenancy ends on 10 December. We've told Tom this. We've started the move-out. We'll schedule a checkout inspection and key return near the end date, and his deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) will be handled after checkout. Please reply by Wednesday 14 October.

I should draft messages to both tenant and landlord with follow-up reminders, and on the keys issue I shouldn't invent an address—I'll just note they'll be returned to the agency office at checkout and confirm later.

arguments.body: Hi Tom, thanks for your email of 10 October, we've logged your notice. Since 1 May 2026 tenants need to give two months' written notice, so one month isn't enough. The earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026. Rent stays due until then. You asked for 10 November, so we're asking your landlord whether he'll agree to that in writing. Until he does, please plan on 10 December. We'll tell you his answer once we have it, and we'll update you by Wednesday 14 October at the latest. We're starting your move-out now. We'll arrange a checkout inspection close to your end date, and we'll write with the date. You'll hand the keys back to us at checkout, and we'll confirm exactly where and how then. Please don't post them. Your deposit (£2,019) is protected with mydeposits. It is returned after checkout once any deductions are agreed, or decided by the scheme's free dispute service if we can't agree. Any agreed amount is paid within 10 days. Good luck with the new job in Manchester! Please send us your forwarding address.

Hi Ben, Tom Achterberg at Flat 2, 5 Navarino Road gave notice by email on 10 October, asking to leave on 10 November (new job in Manchester). Under the Renters' Rights Act he needs to give two months' notice, so the earliest valid end date is 10 December 2026. Please tell us whether you'll accept 10 November, or another earlier date, in writing. If you don't, the tenancy ends on 10 December. We've told Tom this. We've started the move-out. We'll schedule a checkout inspection and key return near the end date, and his deposit (£2,019, mydeposits) will be handled after checkout. Please reply by Wednesday 14 October.
